chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the maʾmūmah wound, and he said: “One-third of the diyah; and the jāʾifah wound is one-third of the diyah.” And I asked him about the mūḍiḥah, and he said: “Five camels.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation payable for bodily injury or homicide
key_terms.الشَّجَّةُ الْجَائِفَةُ: a penetrating wound reaching an inner cavity of the body, carrying one-third of the diyah
key_terms.الشَّجَّةِ الْمَأْمُومَةِ: a head wound reaching the membrane surrounding the brain, for which a fixed compensation is given
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.خَمْسٌ مِنَ الْإِبِلِ: the prescribed compensation of five camels

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed diyah for the maʾmūmah, jāʾifah, and mūḍiḥah wounds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding compensation for specific bodily injuries. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that the compensation for the maʾmūmah and the jāʾifah wounds is one-third of the diyah, while the compensation for the mūḍiḥah is five camels.
